sections.html: Gymnochanda ploegi is a tiny, scaleless glass perch. Maximum size is about 2.8 cm standard length. IUCN Red List: Data Deficient.

It comes from the Sanggau and Kapuas Lakes areas of West Kalimantan, Borneo. It was described in 2014 by Tan and Lim and named for Alex Ploeg, Secretary General of Ornamental Fish International, who died on flight MH17 that year.
It lives in still pools near swamp forest and river systems, in soft, acidic water with dense vegetation and low light. Habitat: still pools near peat swamp forest.
Gentle flow, soft light and floating plants for cover. Very delicate and intolerant of poor water quality or high mineral content.

• TDS: 20 to 90 ppm
  • pH: 5.0 to 6.5. Absolutely no salt.
  • Temperature: 24 to 28°C; keep stable and well oxygenated
Micro-predator. Microworms, daphnia, newly hatched brine shrimp and small insects. Once settled, may take finely chopped frozen foods or micro granules.

Peaceful. Keep in groups of 6 or more. Only house with very small, peaceful soft-water species such as Boraras, tiny tetras, kuhli loaches and small shrimp. Avoid fast or aggressive fish and livebearers.

Body: small, transparent, scaleless; the swim bladder and spine are visible. Mature males have expanded second dorsal and anal fins with elongated rays, are pinkish with red on the upper half, with maroon-red dorsal and anal fins edged in black and a red-tinted tail. Females have no fin extensions and are yellowish with reddish tints and mostly clear.
Captive breeding is difficult due to the tiny fry and specialized spawning behavior.
